notes: E6 test case dataset. Two state tenants of 500 field workers, eight NGO tenants sharing 500, at day 180. Only encounter volume differs between the three; beneficiary population does not grow with programme activity. bundle_path and bundle_revision must be filled in before generating. A tenant may also carry its own bundle_path, which is how H1's 'cover the range of organisation size' is done -- config size drives the syncDetails row count -- without them this recipe cannot be reproduced. Organisation ids recorded 6 Oct 2026, after provisioning: state-1 and state-2 already existed at 10 and 11, and ngo-1 to ngo-8 were created with the server assigning 12 to 19 -- read back from GET /organisation rather than inferred from the sequence. They held 1-10 before, which named four live organisations; see docs/execution-plan.md. supervisor_level is Taluka, not the TenantSpec default of Sub-Centre: the bundle's hierarchy has no Sub-Centre, and after `from_target_types` truncates at the deepest permitted registration type the chain is State > District > Taluka > Village. Taluka is the tier above a field worker's village, which is what the scenarios mean by supervision one tier up. states-day-180 has carried this since it was built; the pilots inherited the default and would have failed at `cat.plan`. **This variant fixes the supervisor span at 20 workers each** -- the high end of the 8-to-20 range the scenarios sweep, giving 25 state supervisors and 3 per NGO tenant, 1,580 users. The span is not a run property: it changes how many supervisors exist and how wide each catchment is, and both are structural rows, so switching spans is a reload rather than a flag. Span 8 reproduces the scenarios' own 1,504 workers and 188 supervisors, which is how we know that table assumed the low end. It was generated and then dropped on 6 Oct 2026: 63 supervisors per state tenant against 8.4's 60 is 5%, and the measured establishment already sits almost on the low end, so the two points worth running are pilot-day-180 at 8.4 and this one at 20.
